correctness_confidence.basis: Checkable mathematical claims (Sec. 2 bullets, Table 1 algebraic/combinatorial statements) and exact finite-field quantities (C01 J_{3,2}(I_2)=165,625 and 53/78,125, C03 1225, C04 4096, C09 TV=4/5, C11, C13-C16 budgets, Figs. 1-3) verify cleanly; minor Table 1 omissions (Q in row 6, r in row 4) and externalized code lower confidence from 5 to 4.

novelty.basis: All main mathematical theorems and obstructions (Thms. 1-4, Props. 9, 13, 21, 26, Cor. 3, App. B.2) originate in Lewko [1]; the manuscript contributes constructive Lean 4.35.0 parameter-budget proofs (including the universal eta >= 1/8 corollary at rho = 1/k) and 16 exact zero-float finite-field witness certificates.

reproducibility.basis: Sec. 5 specifies deterministic build/audit commands, MANIFEST.sha256, and 33 unit/forgery/AST tests; however, the PDF omits the Lean/Python source files and full defining data for several certificates (subspaces in C06-C08, affine shift in C10, set S in C12, and n,s in C14-C15), preventing self-contained verification from the PDF alone.

rigor.basis: Constructive proofs of prop13_cauchy_davenport_bound, wan_zhang_betti_bound, and eta_one_eighth_universal are sound, and Sec. 1 candidly states the formalization boundary; however, Table 1 omits domain quantifiers (n >= 2, d >= 0, s >= 1, eta_den > 0), leaves Q (row 6) and r (row 4) undefined, and Sec. 1 writes p^{r/D+1} where Fig. 2 and C06 use p^{floor(r/D)+1}.

significance.basis: Provides an immediate machine-checked parameter-budget audit and concrete small-field obstruction and active-extractor witnesses (C01-C16) supporting Lewko's breakthrough [1], though deep analytic and additive-combinatorial engines ([2], [4], [5]) remain unformalized external theorems.

potential_errors: Table 1 row 6 (prop9_a_below_half_kp1) writes 4*D*tau <= Q => a = k/2 + D*tau < (k+1)/2 without defining Q; for arbitrary Q > 1 this is false unless Q = 1 or tau denotes a numerator over denominator Q (in which case a = k/2 + D*tau lacks /Q).
Table 1 row 4 (endpoint_Ih_subspace_sharpness) states k >= 2, h >= 1, k(h-1)+2 <= n => 2r < (k+1)n /\ r < Dh without specifying r = k + D(h-1) in the theorem summary.

Table 1 omits domain/positivity hypotheses in short summaries: k >= 1 and eta_den > 0 in row 5, s >= 1 in row 11, d >= 0 in row 12 (supplied in Sec. 2 text), n >= 2 in row 14 (without which min(n, 1+X) <= n-1 iff X <= n-2 fails under Nat truncated subtraction at n=0,1), and k >= 1 in row 18.

Theorem 4 in Sec. 1 gives the subspace-evasiveness upper bound with factor p^{r/D + 1}, whereas Fig. 2 (caption and Right panel) and Table 2 (C06) use p^{floor(r/D) + 1} without noting the tightening between continuous and integer exponents.
strengths: Honest, explicit 'Boundary of formalization' in Sec. 1 clearly separates the 18 formalized combinatorial/parameter-budget lemmas from unformalized deep external results ([2], [4], [5]).

All checkable exact finite-field quantities in Table 2 and Figs. 1-3 are algebraically and numerically consistent upon independent recalculation, including J_{3,2}(I_2) = 165,625 and ||mu^{*3}||_2^2 = 53/78,125 in F_{5^5} (C01-C02), J_{2,2}(F_{25}) = 1225 (C03), char-2 Frobenius collapse J_{2,2}(F_{2^4}) = 4096 (C04), CD sums in C05-C07, Wan-Zhang bound in C08, TV = 4/5 in C09, Cor. 27 pairing max 128 < 263/2 in C11, and Prop. 9/Cor. 3 budgets in C13-C16.

Constructive proof sketches in Sec. 2 for Proposition 13's Hou-Leung-Xiang dimension bound, Theorem 19's Wan-Zhang Betti inequality via C(2N,N) < 4^N, and the uniform eta >= 1/8 saving at rho = 1/k are mathematically sound.

Strong alignment across Abstract, Table 1, Table 2, and all six panels of Figures 1-3 (with C13, C15, C16 accurately placed on the eta(k, gamma) curves in Fig. 1 Right and exact point counts matching Fig. 2 Right and Fig. 3 Left).
strong_novelty_candidates: Constructive Lean 4.35.0 formalization (zero sorry, zero Classical.choice, zero custom axioms) of the combinatorial and rational parameter-budget core of Lewko [1], including an explicit universal saving eta >= 1/8 at rho = 1/k for all k >= 2 when p > (24k+12)^{4k(k+1)}.
Zero-float exact F_{p^n} = F_p[T]/(f(T)) verification suite auditing 16 concrete obstruction, moment-curve sharpness, extractor affine-span, and parameter-budget certificates (C01-C16).
summary: This 5-page companion paper presents a constructive Lean 4.35.0 formalization of 18 combinatorial, algebraic, and rational parameter-budget lemmas from Mark Lewko's paper on the finite-field Vinogradov system and polynomial two-source extractors (arXiv:2611.34837v1), together with a zero-float exact finite-field verifier auditing 16 concrete witness certificates (C01-C16) across four modes. The manuscript clearly states its formalization boundary, explicitly treating deep external ingredients (Marton's conjecture, Bourgain-Gamburd flattening, Wan-Zhang Betti bounds, and Wooley's efficient congruencing) as external theorems. Independent checking of the stated theorems and all computable numerical/algebraic quantities in Table 2 and Figures 1-3 confirms complete consistency, with only minor presentation/quantifier omissions in Table 1 summaries and the omission of source code and some witness parameters from the PDF itself.
weaknesses: The Lean 4.35.0 source code, Python verifier, and full input specifications for several certificates (subspace equations in C06-C08, affine shift/projection in C10, set S in C12, and n, s in C14-C15) are not included in the PDF, preventing fully self-contained verification from the manuscript alone.

Several of the 18 Lean theorems in Table 1 (e.g., rows 1, 2, 10, 13, 15, 16, 17) are elementary 1-line arithmetic or definitional identities, so the headline count of 18 formalized theorems somewhat overstates the formalization depth relative to the deeper unformalized analytic results of [1].

In Section 2 bullet 1 (Prop. 13), the induction proof sketch writes D * sum >= D*r + k rather than the cleaner equivalent sum >= r + 1 (valid for D >= k >= 1), without clarifying the induction parameter when 2r < (k+1)n couples k, r, and n.
